title: PR #14 — Encrypted cache, outbox, sync engine, and key lifetime
description: Make the vault usable offline and fast: cache ciphertext and metadata in IndexedDB, queue mutations in an outbox, reconcile conflicts, and keep the vault key only in memory with a strict lock lifecycle. Requirement IDs: TASK-36, TASK-37.
acceptanceCriteria: IndexedDB stores items, folders, wrapped key material, sync state, and an outbox; no plaintext item content is ever persisted
`vaultKey` lives in a module-scoped variable, never in React state, localStorage, sessionStorage, or IndexedDB plaintext
Reloading the page after unlock renders from cache without a network request
An offline create survives reload and syncs exactly once after reconnect
Mutations flush in order and stop on the first failure, preserving the queue
A 409 conflict triggers a refetch and surfaces a visible conflict notice rather than overwriting
Logout and account switch wipe every store, including the wrapped key
Switching between vault routes does not prompt for the password again
The manual lock action works from any vault route

steps.details: Create `app/lib/vault/local-db.ts` using idb with stores: `items` (key id, index by rev), `folders`, `keys` (userId, wrappedVaultKey, wrapSalt, kdfSalt, kdfIterations), `sync` (userId → serverRev, cursor), `outbox` (auto-increment id, op, payload, queuedAt), `meta` (preferences). Add an `openDb()` that creates stores on upgrade and a `wipeDb()`.

Create `app/lib/vault/key-store.ts` holding the unwrapped `vaultKey` in a module variable with `setKey`, `getKey` (throws when locked), `clearKey`. Never expose it through context values that could be serialized; expose only `isUnlocked` and operations that use it internally.

Create `app/lib/vault/cache.ts` with `putItems`, `putFolders`, `getAllItems`, `getAllFolders`, `deleteItem`, `applyTombstone`, each operating on ciphertext and metadata only. Decryption happens in a separate selector layer that takes the key from `keyStore`.

Create `app/lib/vault/sync.ts` with `sync()` that reads `serverRev`, calls `/api/vault?since=`, applies items and tombstones to the cache, updates `serverRev` and cursor, and loops until no `nextCursor`. Skip work when offline and expose a `syncStatus` observable for the UI.

Create `app/lib/vault/outbox.ts` with `enqueue(op)`, `flush()` that processes entries in order, stops on the first network error, and retains failures for retry. On success, update the cached row with the server-returned rev. On 409, drop the optimistic change, trigger a refetch, and emit a conflict event.

On lock, clear the in-memory key and any decrypted selector cache but keep ciphertext stores and wrapped keys. On logout, call `wipeDb()` and clear the key. On login as a different user, wipe before writing new keys. Verify with an IndexedDB inspector that no plaintext remains.

Vitest with fake-indexeddb: enqueue offline create, reopen the database, flush once, assert a single POST; simulate 409 and assert refetch plus conflict event. Playwright: unlock, go offline, create an item, reload, go online, assert the item exists server-side once.

technicalNotes: Never cache decrypted item objects; decrypt on read into component scope.
Outbox operations must be idempotent from the server's perspective; use client-generated ids for creates so a retry after an ambiguous failure does not duplicate.
IndexedDB may be unavailable in private mode; degrade to online-only with a clear notice.
Do not use localStorage for keys or item data, even encrypted, because it is synchronous and easily leaked by XSS.
This PR has no visual design work; it exposes hooks and status for TASK-14 and later.
